strings.help_text:
BASIC SHAPE
app:
  name: My app
pages:                  # each page = a tab
  - title: Ping
    items:              # page elements, top to bottom
      - field: site     # input field
        label: Site
        type: host      # text | host | number | choice
        placeholder: google.com   # faint hint while the field is empty
        default: ""               # default value (optional)
      - button: Start
        run: ping {site} -c 4     # {site} is taken from the field

FIELDS
type: text    any text (escaped automatically)
type: host    IP or domain only
type: number  integer only
type: choice  options: { IPv4: "-4", IPv6: "-6" }

BUTTONS AND COMMANDS
- button: Title
  run: command            # one command
  confirm: true           # ask first (or confirm: "your text")
  reboot: true            # after the command, wait for the reboot and reconnect

COMMAND CHAINS AND FALLBACKS
  run:
    - cmd: service dropbear restart
      ok_if: ""            # text that must appear in the reply (else failure)
      fail_if: "not found" # text that marks failure if present
      fallback:            # runs if this step failed
        - service ssh restart
    - cmd: echo done
      when: ok             # ok (default) | failed | always
      when_contains: ""    # run only if the previous reply contains this text
      when_not_contains: ""
A step fails if exit code is not 0, ok_if is missing or fail_if is present.

CHECKING THAT COMMANDS EXIST
Before showing a button, the app checks on the device that its first command exists
(for example service or ubus). If not, the button is not shown. Chains with a fallback
are shown if at least one of the commands exists. Manually: requires: [ubus, jsonfilter]
(or requires: false to skip the check). A page with no suitable element is hidden.

PROGRESS BAR
- progress: Memory
  source: memory          # memory | disk
  path: /tmp              # disk only (default /overlay or /)
  unit: auto              # auto | KB | MB | GB
  # or your own: run: a command printing 'total used' in bytes

TABLE FROM COMMAND OUTPUT (list)
- list: Services
  run: ls /etc/init.d     # each output line = one table row
  name: '^(\S+)'          # optional regular expression (group 1 or whole match)
  search: true            # search box
  filter: { label: Running only, var: state, is: running }
  columns:                # extra columns, one command per column
    - title: State
      var: state          # variable name for buttons and conditions
      run: |              # {names} = all names separated by spaces; print lines 'name value'
        for n in {names}; do echo "$n ..."; done
      values: { running: "● running", stopped: "○ stopped" }  # nicer labels
    - titles: [CPU %, RAM %]   # one command can fill several columns
      vars: [cpu, mem]
      run: ...
  actions:                # buttons in every row
    - label: Start
      run: /etc/init.d/{name} start     # {name} and column variables: {state}, {pid}…
      enabled_if: { var: state, is: stopped }   # greyed out until the condition holds
      show_if: { var: boot, is_not: enabled }   # hidden until the condition holds
      confirm_for: [dropbear, network]  # ask for confirmation for these names
      confirm: "Really terminate {name}?"       # or always ask
      hint: tooltip text
Conditions: is, is_not, empty: true|false. See the Services tab of the example for a full OpenWrt service list.

LANGUAGES
Folder lang: ru.json, en.json. Your own: copy a file, translate the values (keep the keys), press “＋” next to the language selector. name = display name, flag = flag emoji, strings = translations. Texts inside the YAML description are written by its author and are not translated.
